title: Demand Service Rate Programs: Crediting the Owner for a Response Commitment Not Kept
content:
## The situation this covers

Where a response commitment was not kept on one demand call under the Demand Service Rate Programs, the
owner stands to be given money back on the demand service account for that call.

The credit for a missed response is worked out only once the labor charge for the call it arises from stands invoiced on the demand service account. Until such a labor charge stands invoiced on that account for the call, the credit is
not worked out.

## The effect on the account

One demand service credit entry is opened on the rate program, marked as a missed response credit,
carrying the work order of the call it arises from, the money amount credited and the day it was issued.
That amount comes off what the owner owes on the demand service account and shows on the work order as a
credit.

## Issuing the credit

The desk handles this itself. The tool `credit_missed_response_9859bc76` is unlocked and then called by
the agent, with the money amount credited worked out from the published terms and the records and passed
in; the tool opens the credit entry and neither works the figure out nor judges whether the terms allow
it.

## The parameters

| Parameter | What it is |
|---|---|
| `program_id` | The reference number of the demand service rate program the credit is issued on, read from the rate program lookup on the account. |
| `work_order_ref` | The work order number of the call the credit arises from, written as WO- followed by 7 digits, exactly as it stands on the call record in the demand service history. |
| `credit_amount_usd` | The money amount credited to the owner, in USD to 2 decimal places, rounded half up at the cent and never negative. |

## The receipt

The call returns one line of plain text naming the reference number of the new demand service credit
entry, the work order it was issued against and the credited amount in USD to 2 decimal places. The
named credit entry reference is the receipt that the credit was issued.
